title: Leaseback warm-pool and utilization-proxy: reduce cold-start jitter and unify utilization signals
author: Samantha Ortiz
description: Context and motivation: customer tenants with bursty short-lived traffic observed frequent cold-start spikes despite warm pools sized by static heuristics. Current warm pools are per-cluster and use LRU eviction which doesn't respect tenant burst budgets, causing unfairness and surprising latency spikes for tenants that recently paid for reserved capacity. This PR introduces a lease-backed warm pool allocator plus a utilization-proxy telemetry component to (1) reduce cold-start jitter by holding short-term leases for tenants who request burst capacity, (2) decouple warm-pool lifetime from raw LRU so tenant-level agreements and soft-return windows are respected, and (3) export a normalized utilization proxy across heterogeneous GPU types for better autoscaler decisions.
summary: Implements lease-backed warm pool (controller + runtime hooks), soft-return window for leases, per-tenant burst-debt accounting, and a utilization-proxy exporter that normalizes GPU footprints and reports per-tenant warm efficiency metrics to the metrics pipeline.

diff_highlights: New CRD-like in-memory Lease structure: contains tenant_id, lease_id, acquired_at, duration, soft_return_window, and debt_marker
Controller: reconciliation now assigns warmlet instances to tenants by creating a lease rather than marking an instance 'reserved' in the old LRU list
Runtime: added lease gRPC endpoints to acquire/release and a non-blocking 'renew' call that returns a probabilistic extension to cut frequency of churn
Autoscaler: utilization-proxy takes raw GPU metrics + model footprint and outputs a normalized 'proxy-units' metric used by headroom estimator
Eviction: eviction policy changed to respect soft-return windows and per-tenant minimum lease floor before reclaiming
Console: new UI table and per-tenant charts for warm-pool efficiency and 'burst debt' over time
Docs: operator tuning guide with recommended lease durations, soft-return windows, and impact on billing metrics
test_plan: Unit tests for lease logic and eviction ordering; integration e2e that simulates 100 tenants with bursty traffic verifying P95 tail latency improves and cold-start events decrease; a smoke test for utilization-proxy exposing consistent values across two GPU families (A100 and H100 profiles). CI ran integration stage with a simulated cluster; one flaky e2e was rerun and passed.
performance_notes: In a staged perf run with 200 simulated tenants we saw cold-start tail latency (P99) drop by ~37% for microburst flows while warm-pool memory overhead increased by ~4% due to short leases. Autoscaler contamination reduced because utilization-proxy decouples raw GPU % from model-kernel footprint.
operator_notes: Default lease duration set to 90s with soft-return-window 30s. Operators can tune via Helm chart (charts/redwood/values.yaml). Lease decisions are idempotent and safe to roll back: controller will mark leases as expired and return warmlets to the common pool. Deprecated flags: warmpool-size-static is still supported but superseded when leaseback enabled.
review_thread: Rajesh: Can you explain how leases interact with Dedicated reserved capacity? If a tenant holds a lease but has an active reserved pool, do we double-count their allocation?

Samantha: Good question. Leases are orthogonal — if a tenant has reserved capacity the lease will preferentially allocate from their reserved warmlets; the debt_marker records whether the warmlet was served from reserved vs shared. The utilization-proxy includes a 'source' dimension so downstream billing and autoscaler logic can subtract reserved footprint.
Linus: Eviction ordering needs stronger tests for rare race windows where renewals and eviction collide.
Samantha: Added two edge-case e2e tests (lease_renewal_race and eviction_during_renew) and fixed a race in lease_reconciler by making the compare-and-swap idempotent.
Mei: The normalized units algorithm is neat but we need a note about how we map quantized models (4-bit) vs fp16 — are we penalizing quantized models for lower raw GPU utilization?

Samantha: The normalizer uses a model-footprint heuristic combined with measured kernel throughput; quantized models typically show lower GPU occupancy but similar effective throughput — we run a per-model calibration sample during onboarding and store a footprint coefficient which the proxy uses. Added docs and a calibration job script.
ci_summary: Checks: unit-tests (pass), linters (pass), integration/e2e (pass after 1 rerun), qa-smoke (pass), security-scan (pass). Flaky e2e was transient and re-run by CI bot. Build artifacts published to internal registry.
merge_outcome: merged via squash (squash and merge). Commit message condensed to: 'leaseback warm pool + utilization proxy: lease controller, runtime endpoints, proxy exporter, UI and docs'
release_notes: Added lease-backed warm pool allocator to reduce cold-start jitter for bursty tenants; introduced utilization-proxy metric to normalize utilization across GPU families; operator tunables for lease duration and soft-return window. Backwards compatible; opt-in via Helm flag 'warmpool.leaseback.enabled'.
